newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait oil chief to visit KPC refineries abroad.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait oil chief to visit KPC refineries abroad.

text.p: Kuwait's Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi flew to the Netherlands and Italy to inspect Kuwait's downstream operations in Europe, al-Anba newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The daily said Mazeedi plans to visit Kuwaiti refineries, fuel stations and storage facilities in Europe during the tour and meet with Dutch and Italian officials.
In October Kuwait finalised a deal with Agip SpA for a 50 percent share in the Italian firm's Milazzo refinery and the purchase of 330 fuel stations.
Experts earlier said the two sides planned to upgrade the refinery and increase its capacity from 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 240,000 bpd.
Kuwait's only other oversees refinery is in Rotterdam with an 80,000 bpd capacity. Last year Kuwait said it would close its uncompetitive 59,000 bpd refinery in Denmark.
Al-Anba said Kuwait's 349 fuel stations in Luxembourg, Belgium and the Netherlands account for a 3.6 percent share of the market or 50,000 bpd.

Kuwait, which has a daily OPEC quota of two million bpd, has a domestic refining capacity of about 895,000 bpd. It is actively involved in talks and plans to set up or participate in refineries mainly in Asia to increase state revenue by selling higher-value refined products.
